meta.titre: Pressure: force on an area, from knives to lorry tyres

sections.contenu_markdown: A heavy lorry loaded with cocoa sacks sinks into the soft mud of a rain-soaked road near Kumba, while a motorbike taxi with a much lighter load rides over the same spot. A farmer sharpens his machete because a sharp edge cuts better than a blunt one. In each case the key is not only the force, but how that force is spread over an area. Pressure questions appear every year at the GCE O/L, often as short calculations and as explanations of everyday objects.

items: Weight is mass multiplied by $g$, with $g = 10\ \mathrm{N\,kg^{-1}}$.
Area of a rectangle is length times width, and $1\ \mathrm{cm^2} = 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m^2}$.

sections.contenu_markdown:
**Pressure** is the force acting normally (at right angles) on a surface per unit area of that surface:

$$P = \frac{F}{A}$$

- $F$ is the force in newtons (N) and $A$ is the area in square metres ($\mathrm{m^2}$).
- The SI unit is the **pascal** (Pa): $1\ \mathrm{Pa} = 1\ \mathrm{N\,m^{-2}}$.
- For a body resting on a horizontal surface, the force on the surface is its weight, $F = mg$.

The same force gives a **larger** pressure on a **smaller** area. Pressure can therefore be changed in two ways: by changing the force or by changing the area.

| Aim | What to do | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Increase pressure | make the area small | a nail point, a sharp knife, high-heeled shoes |
| Decrease pressure | make the area large | wide tractor tyres, snowshoes, double wheels on a heavy truck, the wide foundation of a building |

Always convert areas to $\mathrm{m^2}$ before dividing. Remember that $1\ \mathrm{cm^2} = 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m^2}$, not $10^{-2}\ \mathrm{m^2}$.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the same object stands on a different face and you must compare the pressures.
variantes.contenu_markdown: The force (weight) is the same for every face, but the area in contact changes. The face with the **smallest** area gives the **greatest** pressure, and the face with the largest area gives the least. Calculate the area of the face in contact each time and use $P = F/A$.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the load is carried by many wheels or feet.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Total area in contact $=$ number of wheels (or feet) $\times$ area of each. Standing on one foot halves the area, so the pressure on the ground is doubled for the same weight. Doubling the number of wheels of a heavy truck halves the pressure on the road, which reduces damage to the road surface.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks about a pressure cooker (pressure pot).
variantes.contenu_markdown: In a sealed pot the steam cannot escape, so the pressure above the water increases. At higher pressure, water boils at a temperature above $100\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The food is cooked at a higher temperature, so it cooks faster and saves fuel.

sections.enonce_markdown: A rectangular concrete block of mass $12\ \mathrm{kg}$ has dimensions $0.50\ \mathrm{m} \times 0.40\ \mathrm{m} \times 0.30\ \mathrm{m}$. Calculate the pressure it exerts on the ground (a) when it rests on its largest face and (b) when it rests on its smallest face. Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{N\,kg^{-1}}$.

etapes.action: Find the weight of the block.
etapes.justification: The force on the ground is the weight, $F = mg$.

etapes.action: Find the area of the largest face.
etapes.justification: The largest face is the one with the two longest edges, $0.50$ and $0.40$.

etapes.action: Find the pressure on the largest face.
Find the area of the smallest face and the pressure on it.
etapes.justification: The smallest face has the two shortest edges, $0.40$ and $0.30$; the weight is unchanged.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The pressure is **600 Pa** on the largest face and **1000 Pa** on the smallest face: the smaller area gives the larger pressure.

items.erreur_markdown: A student converts an area of $150\ \mathrm{cm^2}$ into $1.5\ \mathrm{m^2}$ by dividing by $100$.
items.pourquoi_faux: One square metre is $100 \times 100 = 10\,000\ \mathrm{cm^2}$, so the conversion factor for area is $10^4$, not $10^2$.

items.erreur_markdown: A student uses the mass of a body in kilograms as the force in $P = F/A$.
items.pourquoi_faux: The force on a surface is the weight in newtons, not the mass in kg.
items.correction_markdown: First calculate $F = mg$, then divide by the area.

items.erreur_markdown: A student says: "A wide tyre exerts more pressure because it touches more ground."
items.pourquoi_faux: For the same load, a bigger contact area spreads the force, so the pressure is smaller.
items.correction_markdown: State that a larger area gives a smaller pressure, for the same force.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes the pressure of a block as $600\ \mathrm{N}$.
items.pourquoi_faux: N is the unit of force. Pressure is force per area, measured in Pa ($\mathrm{N\,m^{-2}}$).

items.enonce_markdown: A girl of mass $45\ \mathrm{kg}$ stands on level ground. The area of the sole of each of her shoes in contact with the ground is $150\ \mathrm{cm^2}$. Calculate the pressure she exerts on the ground (a) standing on both feet and (b) standing on one foot. Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{N\,kg^{-1}}$.
items.solution_markdown:
Weight: $F = 45 \times 10 = 450\ \mathrm{N}$. Each foot: $150\ \mathrm{cm^2} = 150 \times 10^{-4} = 0.015\ \mathrm{m^2}$.

(a) Both feet: $A = 2 \times 0.015 = 0.03\ \mathrm{m^2}$, so $P = \dfrac{450}{0.03} = 15\,000\ \mathrm{Pa}$. **Pressure = 15 000 Pa.**

(b) One foot: $P = \dfrac{450}{0.015} = 30\,000\ \mathrm{Pa}$. **Pressure = 30 000 Pa**, twice as much because the area is halved.

items.enonce_markdown: A loaded lorry weighs $80\,000\ \mathrm{N}$ and rests on $8$ tyres. The contact area of each tyre with the road is $0.10\ \mathrm{m^2}$. (a) Calculate the pressure on the road. (b) Calculate the pressure if the same lorry had only $4$ such tyres, and say how many times greater it is.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Total area $= 8 \times 0.10 = 0.80\ \mathrm{m^2}$. $P = \dfrac{F}{A} = \dfrac{80\,000}{0.80} = 100\,000\ \mathrm{Pa}$. **Pressure = 100 000 Pa.**

(b) Total area $= 4 \times 0.10 = 0.40\ \mathrm{m^2}$. $P = \dfrac{80\,000}{0.40} = 200\,000\ \mathrm{Pa}$. **Pressure = 200 000 Pa**, which is $2$ times greater, because the area is halved while the weight is the same.

items.enonce_markdown: A thumb presses a drawing pin with a force of $20\ \mathrm{N}$. The flat head has an area of $1.0\ \mathrm{cm^2}$ and the point has an area of $0.050\ \mathrm{mm^2}$. Calculate (a) the pressure on the thumb and (b) the pressure of the point on the wooden board, assuming the whole force reaches the board. (c) How many times larger is the second pressure?
items.solution_markdown:
Convert the areas: $1.0\ \mathrm{cm^2} = 1.0 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m^2}$ and $0.050\ \mathrm{mm^2} = 0.050 \times 10^{-6} = 5.0 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{m^2}$.

(a) $P = \dfrac{20}{1.0 \times 10^{-4}} = 200\,000\ \mathrm{Pa}$. **Pressure on the thumb = $2.0 \times 10^5$ Pa.**

(b) $P = \dfrac{20}{5.0 \times 10^{-8}} = 4.0 \times 10^{8}\ \mathrm{Pa}$. **Pressure on the board = $4.0 \times 10^8$ Pa.**

(c) $\dfrac{4.0 \times 10^8}{2.0 \times 10^5} = 2\,000$. **The point exerts 2000 times the pressure**, which is why the pin enters the wood and does not hurt the thumb.

items_markdown: Pressure $P = F/A$; the SI unit is the pascal, $1\ \mathrm{Pa} = 1\ \mathrm{N\,m^{-2}}$.
On a horizontal surface the force is the weight $F = mg$; always convert the area to square metres first.
A small area gives a large pressure (knife, nail); a large area gives a small pressure (wide tyres, double wheels, snowshoes).
In a pressure cooker the raised pressure raises the boiling point of water, so food cooks faster.
